transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, yeah… thanks. I guess what brought me in is that my eating has gotten kind of… not great. I mean, I usually try to stay pretty on top of things, track my food and all that, but lately I just stopped caring about it.

It wasn’t like I meant to do anything drastic, I just sort of skipped actual meals for a few days and was mostly getting by on coffee and protein bars. Then I noticed my clothes were getting loose, like hanging off me a bit, and I hadn’t really realized it was happening until then. I figured I should probably talk to someone before it gets worse, if that makes sense.
Have you been worried about gaining weight or feeling like you need to lose more weight, even though you’ve already lost some?

I don’t think so… not in that way. I mean, I’m not trying to get thinner or anything, at least I don’t think I am. I guess I just got kind of careless with meals. I know that probably doesn’t sound great, but I’m not, like, aiming for a certain weight or scared of gaining, if that’s what you mean.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound too dramatic, but yes, I think so.

After the sponsor questioned my judgment at work, it kind of… hit me harder than it probably should have. I went home and just sat in my apartment feeling really hollow and embarrassed. I remember crying over emails that, normally, I would’ve just answered and moved on from. It felt shameful, honestly. Like I should’ve been able to handle it better.
Have you felt down or lost interest in things for most of the day, more days than not, over the past couple of weeks?

Yeah… I think, yes. I don’t want to overstate it, but it has felt like that most days.

After the sponsor questioned my judgment, it was like the bottom kind of dropped out. I’d go home and just sit there in my apartment feeling hollow and ashamed, and I was crying over emails I normally would’ve just handled. It’s embarrassing to say, but… yeah, it’s been taking up a lot of the day, more often than not.
Have you noticed a decrease in your appetite or any unintentional weight loss recently, outside of the changes you've described in your eating habits?

Yeah… I guess there has been some of that. I didn’t really set out to lose weight or anything, but my eating kind of went completely off the rails.

I stopped really caring about tracking food, and then I was skipping actual meals for days and just getting by on coffee and protein bars. I didn’t think it was that bad at first, but then my clothes started fitting loose—like hanging off a bit—before I really even noticed. I know that sounds irresponsible.
Have you felt fatigued or noticed a loss of energy nearly every day?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I’ve been tired, but I don’t know if I’d call it nearly every day or something significant.

Some days I feel kind of drained, but I also keep telling myself that’s normal with work and everything. I can still get through things, mostly. Is that the kind of fatigue you mean?
Have you felt like you’re not worth much or felt excessive guilt about things, even when it didn’t make sense?

I don’t know… not in a big dramatic way, I guess.

I mean, I’ve felt bad about how I’ve handled things, and I’ve been pretty hard on myself, but I’m not sure if that counts as “excessive” guilt. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Maybe I’ve been blaming myself more than I should, but… I don’t know. Is that what you mean?
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or felt restless and unable to sit still, more days than not?

Yeah… probably more on the restless side than moving slowly.

I mean, I wouldn’t say I was just pacing for no reason exactly, but sitting still felt almost impossible. I kept jumping between things—building dashboards, rewriting timelines, sending these strategy notes, reorganizing my apartment, starting new project templates… all kind of at once.

At the time I thought I was just being productive, maybe overly motivated, but looking back it was a lot. Is that the kind of restlessness you’re asking about?
Have you experienced any days where you completely lost the desire to eat, or noticed a significant drop in your appetite, even when you weren’t consciously skipping meals?

Yeah… I think that did happen. I didn’t really frame it as “loss of appetite” at first, because I was telling myself I was just busy or focused.

But my eating got pretty out of hand. I stopped caring about tracking food like I normally would, and I was skipping actual meals for days—mostly just coffee and protein bars. I don’t think I was trying to not eat exactly… I just didn’t care about it, or it didn’t register.

And then my clothes started fitting loose, kind of hanging off me, before I really noticed what was going on. So… yeah, I guess that would count, right?
Have you had trouble focusing on tasks, or felt like your thinking slowed down or became unclear?

Yeah… focusing was definitely harder, though I don’t know if I’d call it “slowed down.” It was almost the opposite.

My thoughts were moving really fast, jumping from budget risk to staffing models to AI automation to executive politics, and then back again. I could see all these connections, or at least I thought I could, but I couldn’t really hold onto one thread long enough to finish it cleanly.

So I’d start something and feel like it was important, but then my mind would already be three steps somewhere else. Does that make sense for what you’re asking?
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or so confident that you didn’t sleep much but still felt rested?

Yeah… I mean, I guess so. I didn’t think of it as a problem at the time, honestly.

I was sleeping maybe two or three hours, but then I’d wake up feeling… charged, like I was ready to go. I remember thinking sleep was kind of inefficient, like I’d somehow optimized it out of my schedule.

That sounds a little grandiose when I say it out loud, but at the time it felt positive—like I was just functioning really well. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Have you had any distinct periods where your mood was unusually high, irritable, or you felt like you had so much energy that you were doing things nonstop, maybe even taking on big projects or making big plans, even if others thought it was over the top?

Yeah… there were definitely periods like that. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but for days at a time I felt kind of… unstoppable, like I was seeing things more clearly than everyone else and could fix everything if people would just keep up.

I took on a lot, made some pretty big plans, and at the time it honestly felt brilliant, not excessive. But I also got… more irritable than I’d like to admit. If someone asked what was probably a normal question, or slowed me down, I’d snap at them like they were getting in the way on purpose—like they were sabotaging the whole company or something.

That sounds harsh saying it now. But yes, I think that’s what you’re asking about.
Have you ever had a time when your mood was so high or you had so much energy that it led to serious consequences, like getting into trouble at work or at home, or needing to be hospitalized?

Yeah… I guess it did get to that level, though it’s hard for me to say that without feeling like I’m making myself sound… really bad.

Work basically started falling apart. I was missing handoffs that I normally wouldn’t miss, and I sent out strategy documents that made sense to me at the time, but apparently no one else could really follow them. I thought I was being visionary, but looking back, I can see how disorganized it must have seemed.

And then it got serious enough that my manager and corporate security took me to the emergency department. That part is embarrassing to admit.

At home, too, I wasn’t really keeping up with normal stuff—meals, routines, hobbies, basic things. I kept telling myself I was just focused, but… yeah, I think there were real consequences. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Can you tell me if there was a time when your mood was elevated or you felt unusually irritable for at least four days in a row, where it was noticeably different from your usual self?

Yeah… I think so. There were stretches of several days where I felt almost… unusually capable, like everything I was thinking was brilliant and I could push through anything.

I don’t want to overstate it, but it was definitely not my normal self. And I could get really irritable, too. If someone asked a basic question or slowed me down, I’d snap at them like they were deliberately getting in the way or sabotaging the company.

I know that sounds intense. But yes, it did last for days, and people probably could tell something was different.

I know that sounds intense. But yes, it did last for days, and people probably could tell something was different.
